Dell reported US$60.8 billion of fiscal-2026 ISG revenue; HPE reported US$17.7 billion of fiscal-2025 server revenue; and Supermicro reported US$22.0 billion of fiscal-2025 net sales. Those numbers did not mean the products were directly comparable on every line item, but they showed that Lenovo was operating against larger or faster-growing peers in a segment where component costs remained high and pricing discipline could weaken quickly. [Lenovo FY2025/26 results](https://news.lenovo.com/pressroom/press-releases/fy-2025-26/); [Dell FY2026 results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3); [HPE FY2025 results](https://investors.hpe.com/~/media/Files/H/HP-Enterprise-IR/documents/q4-2025/q4-2025-earnings-press-release.pdf); [Supermicro FY2025 results](https://ir.supermicro.com/news/news-details/2025/Supermicro-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

Margin therefore remained the essential sub-risk. AI-server revenue inflated the top line rapidly, but GPUs still dominated the bill of materials. Lenovo's answer was to push higher-value services, liquid-cooling, storage and broader solution attachment around the hardware. The FY2025/26 numbers showed that strategy had begun to work. They did not yet show how wide the margin moat would become once supply loosened and more capacity entered the market. [Lenovo FY2025/26 results](https://news.lenovo.com/pressroom/press-releases/fy-2025-26/)

## Governance Perception and Controlling Shareholder

Lenovo's governance risk also needed more precise numbers than the earlier draft used. The company's own shareholding page showed that, as of March 31 2025, Legend Holdings owned 31.41 per cent of Lenovo, Yang owned 5.94 per cent, and other directors owned 0.11 per cent. The current board page showed Yang still held the combined chairman-chief executive structure. For some investors that combination represented valuable continuity; for others it remained a structural concentration of authority. [Shareholding Structure](https://investor.lenovo.com/en/ir/shareholding.php); [Board of Directors](https://investor.lenovo.com/en/cg/directors.php)

The larger ownership narrative was real but had to be framed carefully. Legend Holdings' own company introduction said it had been founded in 1984 by 11 researchers, including Liu Chuanzhi, with funding from the Institute of Computing Technology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. That supported the dossier's point about state-adjacent lineage without overstating Lenovo's direct ownership chain. [Legend company introduction](https://www.legendholdings.com.cn/Introduction_en/index.aspx?nodeid=1043)

## Supply Chain and Foreign Exchange

Lenovo's own releases also made clear that supply-chain breadth was both hedge and burden. The company said it operated more than 30 manufacturing sites across 10 markets, a network that gave it flexibility across China, Europe, the Americas and India but also required continued capital, logistics and execution discipline. The biggest industry-wide concentration remained upstream: advanced GPUs, memory and networking silicon were still sourced from a narrow supplier base. [Lenovo FY2025/26 results](https://news.lenovo.com/pressroom/press-releases/fy-2025-26/)

Foreign exchange added another layer of volatility. Lenovo reported in US dollars but incurred costs across renminbi, euro and other currencies; the same diversified footprint that helped on trade policy also increased the number of FX lines management had to hedge. None of this was novel. But in a business whose earnings mix was changing quickly, it remained one of the cleanest ways for reported margins to diverge temporarily from underlying operating execution. [Five-Year Financial Summary](https://investor.lenovo.com/en/financial/five_year_summary.php); [Corporate Information](https://investor.lenovo.com/en/about/corpinfo.php)

chapters.title: ISG AI scaling, PC cycle recovery, SSG services, 2026-2030 horizon
chapters.body:
## The Record Year, and What Came Next

Lenovo did not enter the 2026-2030 horizon from a position of stabilisation at roughly US$57 billion of revenue. It entered from a record base. FY2025/26 revenue reached US$83.1 billion, adjusted net income rose 42 per cent year on year to US$2.0 billion, AI-related revenue accounted for 33 per cent of the total, and all three business groups posted double-digit growth. Any serious forward view therefore had to start from a business that had already recovered its post-Covid drawdown and then exceeded its prior peak. [Lenovo FY2025/26 results](https://news.lenovo.com/pressroom/press-releases/fy-2025-26/); [Five-Year Financial Summary](https://investor.lenovo.com/en/financial/five_year_summary.php)

The architecture of that record year mattered. IDG generated US$58.9 billion of revenue, ISG US$19.2 billion, and SSG crossed the US$10 billion mark for the first time. The earlier draft had treated FY2025 as the base case; the more accurate view by the frozen date was that FY2026 had become the new base year from which the next cycle would be judged. [Lenovo FY2025/26 results](https://news.lenovo.com/pressroom/press-releases/fy-2025-26/)

## ISG: From break-even ambition to full-year profit

The decisive change in outlook sat inside ISG. FY2024/25 had already shown the business breaking even in the second half, with revenue up 63 per cent to US$14.5 billion. FY2025/26 then took the next step: US$19.2 billion of full-year revenue, US$73 million of operating profit, a US$21 billion AI-server pipeline, more than 5,800 customer AI deployments, and annual manufacturing capacity of more than 70,000 racks, including more than 11,000 direct-liquid-cooled racks. [Lenovo FY2024/25 results](https://news.lenovo.com/pressroom/press-releases/fy-2024-25/); [Lenovo FY2025/26 results](https://news.lenovo.com/pressroom/press-releases/fy-2025-26/)

That did not remove competition. Dell's fiscal-2026 ISG revenue of US$60.8 billion remained far larger; HPE and Supermicro were still material rivals; and a meaningful share of absolute AI-server volume continued to bypass branded OEMs through the hyperscaler ODM channel. But Lenovo's position by May 2026 was no longer that of an unproven aspirant. It had become a profitable, scaled AI-infrastructure supplier with a large disclosed pipeline. [Dell FY2026 results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3); [HPE FY2025 results](https://investors.hpe.com/~/media/Files/H/HP-Enterprise-IR/documents/q4-2025/q4-2025-earnings-press-release.pdf); [Supermicro FY2025 results](https://ir.supermicro.com/news/news-details/2025/Supermicro-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx); [Lenovo FY2025/26 results](https://news.lenovo.com/pressroom/press-releases/fy-2025-26/)

## IDG: The PC Cycle and the AI Device Thesis

IDG's role in the outlook also looked different once the numbers were corrected. The business was no longer simply defending a floor. In FY2025/26 it grew 17 per cent to US$58.9 billion; in Q4, PC market share reached a record 24.4 per cent and premium-PC mix reached 50 per cent. Lenovo's investment case for the segment rested on the view that AI PCs, commercial refresh and premium mix could support better economics even if the industry never returned to pandemic-era unit distortions. [Lenovo FY2025/26 results](https://news.lenovo.com/pressroom/press-releases/fy-2025-26/)

The caveat was obvious. Every major vendor now had AI-PC products, and Microsoft's Windows 10 end-of-support timeline was a catalyst for the entire ecosystem, not Lenovo alone. The bullish case for IDG was therefore not just higher unit demand. It was that Lenovo's share leadership, channel reach and services attachment would let it monetise the refresh more effectively than peers. [Lenovo Q1 FY2025/26](https://news.lenovo.com/pressroom/press-releases/q1-fy-2025-26/); [Lenovo FY2025/26 results](https://news.lenovo.com/pressroom/press-releases/fy-2025-26/)

## SSG: The Margin Architecture

SSG remained the quietest but, in some respects, the most strategically valuable leg of the stool. FY2025/26 took annual revenue past US$10 billion; in Q4 the segment grew 19 per cent year on year to US$2.6 billion and reported 22.4 per cent operating margin. The mix also kept improving: Managed Services and Project and Solutions contributed 62 per cent of Q4 revenue, while the AI Library had expanded to more than 60 use cases spanning manufacturing, retail and sports. [Lenovo FY2025/26 results](https://news.lenovo.com/pressroom/press-releases/fy-2025-26/)

That mattered because it was the cleanest mechanism by which Lenovo could turn a hardware cycle into recurring economics. TruScale, device-as-a-service, managed services and AI solution delivery all increased the odds that AI infrastructure would not remain a one-time box sale. If ISG provided the hardware and IDG the installed base, SSG remained the layer most likely to influence long-term valuation multiples. [Lenovo Q1 FY2025/26](https://news.lenovo.com/pressroom/press-releases/q1-fy-2025-26/); [Lenovo FY2025/26 results](https://news.lenovo.com/pressroom/press-releases/fy-2025-26/)

## The 2026-2030 Strategic Posture

Lenovo's posture for 2026-2030 rested on three assumptions. First, that enterprise AI would broaden beyond hyperscalers and convert more pilots into production infrastructure, sustaining ISG growth after the initial training-cluster surge. Second, that AI PCs and commercial refresh would keep IDG at or above a materially higher revenue base than the FY2024 trough. Third, that SSG would keep raising recurring mix and protect margins even if hardware pricing grew more competitive.

The company itself summarised the ambition clearly enough: on May 22 2026 it said it was confident in becoming a **US$100 billion** company within two years. That target was aggressive but no longer fanciful. It sat on top of a record year, a profitable ISG, and a services arm that had just crossed US$10 billion of annual revenue. The unresolved question was not whether Lenovo had reached escape velocity from the post-Covid PC slump. By the frozen date it plainly had. The unresolved question was whether the new mix of AI infrastructure, devices and services could sustain that momentum once the first wave of AI spending normalised. [Lenovo FY2025/26 results](https://news.lenovo.com/pressroom/press-releases/fy-2025-26/)

## D. Business Segment Definitions

**IDG — Intelligent Devices Group.** PCs, smartphones, tablets, workstations and adjacent smart devices. FY2025/26 revenue was US$58.9 billion. [Lenovo FY2025/26 results](https://news.lenovo.com/pressroom/press-releases/fy-2025-26/)
